investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-03T17:48–17:56Z because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler with "Unschedulable": the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the agent pod never left the Pending state, so the eval runner could not reach a ready state and the expected-output contract was fully unmet.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents swarm has exhausted the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on the 2 nodes that are eligible for remote agent pods. The scheduler message "2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm" and "No preemption victims found" confirms no capacity is available and no lower-priority pods can be evicted to make room. The remaining 4 nodes are ineligible due to node affinity/selector mismatch. Because the pod never schedules, the agent VM is never provisioned, and the eval runner receives no vmIdPresent or remoteState signal, causing a complete contract gap. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so impact to production end-users cannot be confirmed from this packet alone.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState oneOf [running, idle, ready] — neither assertion can be evaluated because the pod never scheduled.
possibleCauses: [Highest confidence] kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhausted on the 2 eligible nodes: all available VM slots are occupied by existing remote agent pods or other workloads, leaving no capacity for new scheduling attempts. Preemption is blocked because no lower-priority victims exist.

[High confidence] Node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift on 4 of 6 nodes: the remote agent pod spec targets a specific node label or taint that only 2 nodes satisfy, concentrating all scheduling pressure on those 2 nodes and amplifying the capacity exhaustion.

[Medium confidence] Cluster under-provisioning: the total kata.peerpods.io/vm quota across the 2 eligible nodes is too small for the concurrent eval probe load plus any live workloads, causing transient or sustained exhaustion.

[Low confidence] A peer-pod provider-side quota or API limit (upstream of the Kubernetes extended resource) is preventing new VM slots from being advertised to the node, making the resource appear exhausted even if physical capacity exists.

investigation.title: Remote Agent Pods Unschedulable Due to Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity on Production Kubernetes Cluster
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents feature checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api between 17:51 and 17:56 UTC on 2026-07-03 with an identical Kubernetes scheduler message: 0/6 nodes are available, 2 nodes reporting Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm and 4 nodes not matching the pod's node affinity/selector. Because no remote agent pod could be scheduled, the eval runner's createAgent call never returned a live agent, so no evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) was ever written and the expected-output contract was fully unmet.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production remote-agents swarm has exhausted the schedulable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the two nodes that carry that resource label. The remaining four nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector requirements for remote agent workloads. With zero viable nodes and no preemption victims available, every remote agent pod submitted during this window was left in Unschedulable state for ~142–147 seconds before the eval timed out. This is an infrastructure-layer capacity constraint, not an application code defect. No evidence of a user-traffic or production incident signal is present in the packet; the impact is scoped to the AURA observability eval for the remote-agents feature.

Preemption is also blocked ('No preemption victims found'), indicating no lower-priority pods are present to evict.

SECONDARY — node affinity/selector mismatch on the remaining four nodes: the remote agent pod spec requires a node label or taint that only two nodes carry (the kata.peerpods.io/vm nodes), and those two are at capacity. A misconfiguration or unintended label change on those nodes could have reduced effective capacity.

TERTIARY — cluster under-provisioning: the production cluster has only 6 nodes total, with only 2 carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource. If concurrent remote agent demand increased (e.g., from real user traffic or other eval runs), the fixed pool of 2 VM-capable nodes could be saturated.
LOWER CONFIDENCE — a node failure or cordon on one of the two kata.peerpods.io/vm nodes reducing effective capacity from the expected baseline without a corresponding scale-up.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-03T17:48–17:56Z because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler with "Unschedulable": the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the agent pod never left the Pending state, so the eval runner could not reach a ready state and the expected-output contract was fully unmet.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents swarm has exhausted the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on the 2 nodes that are eligible for remote agent pods. The scheduler message "2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm" and "No preemption victims found" confirms no capacity is available and no lower-priority pods can be evicted to make room. The remaining 4 nodes are ineligible due to node affinity/selector mismatch. Because the pod never schedules, the agent VM is never provisioned, and the eval runner receives no vmIdPresent or remoteState signal, causing a complete contract gap. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so impact to production end-users cannot be confirmed from this packet alone.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState oneOf [running, idle, ready] — neither assertion can be evaluated because the pod never scheduled.
possibleCauses: [Highest confidence] kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhausted on the 2 eligible nodes: all available VM slots are occupied by existing remote agent pods or other workloads, leaving no capacity for new scheduling attempts. Preemption is blocked because no lower-priority victims exist.

[High confidence] Node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift on 4 of 6 nodes: the remote agent pod spec targets a specific node label or taint that only 2 nodes satisfy, concentrating all scheduling pressure on those 2 nodes and amplifying the capacity exhaustion.

[Medium confidence] Cluster under-provisioning: the total kata.peerpods.io/vm quota across the 2 eligible nodes is too small for the concurrent eval probe load plus any live workloads, causing transient or sustained exhaustion.

[Low confidence] A peer-pod provider-side quota or API limit (upstream of the Kubernetes extended resource) is preventing new VM slots from being advertised to the node, making the resource appear exhausted even if physical capacity exists.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Kubernetes Pod Scheduling Failure: Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All Three Remote-Agent Checks
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api on 2026-07-03 with identical Kubernetes scheduler errors reporting that 0 of 6 nodes could schedule the eval pod: 2 nodes had insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm resources and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the agent pod never became schedulable, the eval runner's createAgent call (run-status-probes.mjs line 1918) never completed, no evidence was collected, and the expected-output contract for remote-agent-runtime (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) was entirely unmet.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent eval environment exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource capacity on the 2 nodes that support that resource type. The remaining 4 nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity or selector rules. With no schedulable node and no preemption victims available, every remote-agent pod request timed out unscheduled (~142–147 s), preventing agent creation and causing all three remote-agents checks to fail before any runtime evidence could be gathered. This is an eval-infrastructure / cluster-capacity failure localized to the remote-agents Kubernetes scheduling layer; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: the cluster's peer-pod VM quota was fully consumed at the time of the eval run, leaving no capacity for new remote-agent pods. All three sibling checks hit the same condition within a ~5-minute window, consistent with sustained resource exhaustion rather than a transient blip.

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the 4 remaining nodes did not match the pod's affinity/selector rules. If those rules recently changed or if nodes were cordoned, drained, or relabeled, the effective schedulable node count would drop from 6 to 2, amplifying any capacity pressure.

Tertiary — cluster-level quota or limit-range constraint on kata.peerpods.io/vm: a namespace or cluster quota may cap the number of concurrent peer-pod VMs, and concurrent eval runs or other workloads may have consumed the quota before these probes ran.

Lower confidence — transient node pressure or maintenance window: nodes may have been temporarily unavailable due to a rolling upgrade, node drain, or cloud-provider maintenance, reducing schedulable capacity at the time of the eval run. No maintenance or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence to confirm this.

Evidence that the pod spec's node affinity/selector rules were recently changed to exclude the 4 non-matching nodes intentionally would shift the root cause from capacity exhaustion to a configuration change.
